memories.content: Define in one sentence the user groups and usage contexts to which the design knowledge does not apply.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through explicitly excluded targets and situations.
Specify user goals, interaction conditions, and technological constraints under which the proposed design knowledge can be transferred.
Small-scale formative studies can support analytic generalization distinct from statistical representativeness when results are expressed in terms of design conditions and mechanisms.
The author of this proposal tends to apply design knowledge derived from an accessible sample to a broader user population.
Specify field and user data sources and analysis procedures corresponding to all HCI research questions.
In preregistered studies, clarify the criteria for judging plan changes.
In preregistered studies, clarify the location for recording plan changes.
Use a justified minimum-to-maximum target range when confirmations can change, and tie the minimum and maximum to different workload and budget cases.
Specify the observation records, system logs, or interview tools used to collect each type of field and user data.
Specify whether each type of field and user data will be collected before, during, or after deployment.
Readers cannot assess a target range unless both bounds have a stated consequence for schedule, workload, or cost.
In field deployments, network and service instability exist as independent causes of task failure alongside design choices.
If a safety signal occurs in the field system, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over the research schedule and data collection plan.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to its data sources and analysis procedures.
The user authoring this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Define what can still be completed at the minimum target instead of treating every number inside the range as operationally identical.
Use a bounded range to absorb expected confirmation changes without pretending that one early estimate is guaranteed.
Show how session count and facilitator time change at the minimum and maximum bounds.
Define the additional workload or deliverable enabled at the maximum target so the upper bound is not an arbitrary cushion.
A bounded range preserves uncertainty honestly but makes the final workload and budget less certain than one fixed target.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate proposal-quality concerns. The reference focuses on transfer boundaries, analytic generalization, and overgeneralization risk, while the compared frame covers research traceability, preregistration, flexible targets, deployment contingencies, safety precedence, and contribution framing.

relations.reason: These memories state the same one-sided requirement and its review rationale; the compared frame provides no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Explicitly define excluded users and situations so reviewers can judge the generalization boundary.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided claim about positive transfer conditions, distinct from defining exclusions.
relations.summary: Specify the goals, interaction conditions, and technical constraints under which design knowledge transfers.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided methodological claim about the basis and limits of generalization.
relations.summary: Small formative studies may support analytic generalization through stated design conditions and mechanisms without statistical representativeness.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided diagnosis of an authoring tendency, not a shared policy or a counterpart to the compared frame's different contribution-framing tendency.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to generalize design knowledge from an accessible sample to a broader population.

relations.reason: These memories split one documentation requirement into its rationale and the data-source, collection, timing, and analysis details needed for answerability.
relations.summary: Make each research question traceable to specified field or user data, collection instruments and timing, and analysis procedures.

relations.reason: These memories express complementary parts of one one-sided policy for governing preregistration changes.
relations.summary: For preregistered studies, specify both how plan changes are judged and where they are recorded.

relations.reason: These memories restate and elaborate one policy: justify the range, define minimum and maximum consequences, quantify operational differences, and preserve uncertainty honestly.
relations.summary: Use a bounded target range for changing confirmations only when both bounds have explicit deliverable, workload, schedule, or budget implications and the uncertainty tradeoff is acknowledged.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided causal consideration for field deployments.
relations.summary: Treat network and service instability as causes of field-task failure independent of design choices.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful one-sided conditional precedence rule.
relations.summary: When a field-system safety signal occurs, institutional safety procedures override the research schedule and data plan.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided diagnosis concerning contribution framing, operationally different from the reference frame's population-overgeneralization tendency.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame emphasizes traceable data methods, documented preregistration changes, operationally justified target ranges, deployment failure causes, safety precedence, and avoiding feature lists as contributions.
reports.reference_only: The reference defines exclusions and transfer conditions, distinguishes analytic from statistical generalization, and flags extrapolation from accessible samples.
